title: Knowledge check: Building a Delete Endpoint

questions.prompt: What should a create endpoint do after a valid new resource is committed?
options: Return 404 because the new resource did not exist before the request.
Return success before validation and persistence finish.
Let the client set every server-managed identifier and authorization field.
Return a success status appropriate to creation, commonly 201 Created, and identify the new resource when useful.
questions.answer_key: Return a success status appropriate to creation, commonly 201 Created, and identify the new resource when useful.
questions.explanation: Return a success status appropriate to creation, commonly 201 Created, and identify the new resource when useful. This is especially relevant to “Building a Delete Endpoint” because the API contract must remain explicit and reviewable.

questions.prompt: For the lesson “Building a Delete Endpoint”, which check provides the strongest practical evidence?
options: Run one happy-path call and skip invalid, denied, and failure scenarios.
Test against production records so the exercise cannot be repeated safely.
Test persistence and response semantics, including invalid input and missing-resource cases.
Rely on a code review comment without running any representative check.
questions.answer_key: Test persistence and response semantics, including invalid input and missing-resource cases.
questions.explanation: A useful check is repeatable, tied to an observable contract, and includes an important negative or boundary scenario.

questions.prompt: Which review warning is most relevant to “Building a Delete Endpoint”?
options: The API avoids exposing internal secrets and personal data.
A request can mutate state before validation, permission checks, or durable persistence finish.
The expected behavior and relevant failure cases are documented.
A representative test can reproduce the result.
questions.answer_key: A request can mutate state before validation, permission checks, or durable persistence finish.
questions.explanation: This finding weakens a core API guarantee and should be treated as a design or release issue, not only a style concern.
